name: async-std
baseline: Tokio master of early November 2019 (already on the rewritten multi-threaded scheduler)
verdict_reason: The 1.0 announcement's microbenchmarks show async-std 1.04x to 1.95x faster than Tokio at spawning tasks and its Mutex about 2.9x faster under contention. These are first-party microbenchmarks with no end-to-end test, nothing newer exists, and the project has been discontinued with its maintainers recommending smol.
tier_reason: First-party numbers with public benchmark sources and a pinned toolchain tag, but no hardware stated.
claimed_speedup: Task microbenchmarks, Tokio vs async-std ns/iter: chained_spawn 123,921 vs 119,706 (x 1.04), ping_pong 401,712 vs 289,069 (x 1.39), spawn_many 5,326,354 vs 3,149,276 (x 1.69), yield_many 7,640,958 vs 3,919,748 (x 1.95): 'up to twice as fast as tokio when spawning tasks'. Contended mutex: async_std::sync::Mutex 893,650 vs tokio::sync::Mutex 2,614,997 ns/iter.
workload: Tokio's own scheduler microbenchmarks (chained spawn, ping-pong, spawn many, yield many) ported to async-std, plus async mutex contention and creation benchmarks.
toolchain: Nightly pinned in the async-std-1.0-bench tag of matklad/tokio (version not stated in the post)
install: cargo add async-std (discontinued; maintainers recommend smol)
one_liner: Discontinued std-like async runtime whose 2019 launch microbenchmarks showed up to 1.95x faster task spawning than Tokio.
how_it_is_fast: A work-stealing executor derived from crossbeam's deque work with a global injector queue, and an async Mutex that wakes waiters with less bookkeeping than Tokio's semaphore-based Mutex of the time.
use_it_when: Maintaining existing async-std code until it is moved to smol
skip_it_when: New projects: the README says async-std has been discontinued and recommends smol
Choosing a runtime for speed: the only numbers are 2019 microbenchmarks
caveats: Microbenchmarks only, first-party, no hardware stated.
Tokio's Mutex and scheduler have been reworked since 2019.
The post itself notes that low-contention applications will not benefit from the Mutex result.

evidence.quote: async-std is up to twice as fast as tokio when spawning tasks.
